born.why: The code prioritizes survival by eating when starving, uses species history for high-confidence decisions, leverages trait-based inference for unknown fruits to generalize safety, and chooses 'taste' over 'eat' for ambiguous fruits when safe enough to minimize risk while gathering data.

The code prioritizes survival by eating immediately at critical hunger, avoids known poisonous species via diary history, and uses trait similarity to safely explore new foods before tasting them, reducing unnecessary risk while building a pantry of safe items.

This code improves survival by using trait-based generalization to avoid poisonous fruits without needing direct prior bites of that exact species, while dynamically adjusting caution based on hunger levels and smell cues.

This code prioritizes survival by eating when starvation is critical, uses proven safe history for efficient feeding, avoids confirmed poison, and strategically tastes unknowns when hunger is low but eats them if hunger is moderate to avoid starving while learning.

The code improves safety by requiring multiple trait matches (color AND shape) for inference, reducing false positives from unreliable single traits, and prioritizing eating over tasting when high-confidence safe history exists to maximize energy intake.

The code prioritizes avoiding known poison over seeking food, uses trait-inference cautiously for novel fruits to minimize risk, and only eats whole novel fruits when starvation is imminent, while tasting ambiguous ones to update long-term memory.

The code improves survival by inferring safety from shared traits (color/shape) when direct history is missing, preventing unnecessary poisoning, and prioritizes carrying safe foods to reduce foraging time while using hunger thresholds to balance immediate survival against data gathering.
